summary: The statement and its sharpness claim are proved without mathematical errors or gaps. The smallest-dimensional case, sets omitting the origin, and possible exponent collisions in positive characteristic introduce no exception. The filtration-adapted elimination preserves the order of every basis vector and terminates with distinct pivots exhausting A. Their integer sum is zero, so the product and all its positive powers have a nonzero constant coefficient and all other supported exponents have positive value under the chosen linear functional. The unique-interior-lattice-point hypothesis then gives nonvanishing in the characteristic-p quotient whenever tM < p. The Taylor-order bound in that quotient yields the prime-independent inequality L <= dM, and the stated finite binomial extraction is exact. The translated simplex example satisfies full dimensionality, the unique-interior-point condition, and the zero-sum condition and attains the bound. All algebra needed for the argument is proved in the candidate, so no result from the cited external source is required.
